hook.text: Most engines use the Otto cycle, but hybrids rely on a 19th-century trick called the Atkinson cycle.

buildup.text: Atkinson engines hold the intake valve open longer, letting some air escape before compression.

discovery.text: This makes the expansion stroke longer than compression, extracting more energy per fuel drop.

twist.text: The trade-off is less peak power—but electric motors fill the gap perfectly in hybrid cars.

climax.text: Toyota's Prius popularized the Atkinson cycle, proving efficiency could outsell raw power.

punchline.text: Letting air escape on purpose makes the engine more efficient.

quiz.question: Why is the Atkinson cycle more efficient than the Otto cycle?
options: It uses less fuel per injection
Its expansion stroke is longer than compression
